Alicia / Marcus — attaching our initial draft for the SSQ and a dataflow artifact for your review. Highlights / quick notes below; full answers are in the attached docx and CSV subprocessor registry.

Attachments (drafts):
- redwood_privacy_annex_draft_v1.docx (contains DPA annex language, transfer annex options, retention controls)
- dataflow_inference_v2.pdf (architecture/dataflow diagram — hosted vs dedicated vs private overlays)
- subprocessor_registry.csv (current subprocessors, processing regions, purpose)

Key points up front:
- PII classification: we support customer-defined tagging; default system classification (low/medium/high) is applied by ingestion rules and can be overridden.
- Embeddings & model telemetry: embeddings are not persisted by default in hosted mode; customers may opt-in into persistent embedding storage for search use cases — that is documented and controlled by contract.
- Access controls: RBAC at route/model level, tenant-level isolation, audit logs (retained per contract tier).
- KMS: Hosted customers can use envelope encryption with customer-managed data keys (BYOK) — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. For Dedicated/Private deployments, full key custody options including HSM-backed key material are supported.

Open items where we need Horizon input:
1) Confirmation if you require (a) embeddings storage disabled by default, and (b) mandatory BYOK for production data.
2) Any special retention periods for telemetry beyond our baseline of 30 days.

I'll be on the 11/17 call to walk the dataflow and answer questions.

— Marissa

Marissa — thank you for the fast turnaround, the drafts look helpful. A few follow-ups from privacy and procurement before the call:

1) Subprocessors: we need a clear risk score per subprocessor (low/med/high) and whether they process EU personal data. Can you add a column to the registry with risk rationale?
2) Embeddings: Horizon policy is to avoid persistent embeddings unless explicitly approved by legal — please confirm the default is disabled and how customers opt in (UI/contract flag).
3) Telemetry & analytics: please confirm telemetry default retention and whether aggregated analytics are shared with third-party analytics vendors (names and purposes).
4) KMS attestation: Legal requested a KMS attestation document or a short summary of key custody for hosted customers (what we control vs what the customer controls). If you have a one-page attestation PDF that helps.

Procurement also asked about subcontracting notifications and a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors that could access production data.

We can take these on the call 11/17; please confirm the meeting invite.

Best,
Alicia
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Alicia — hi, quick technical clarifications ahead of our call (I can expand on any of these on 11/17):

- Subprocessor risk score: we will add a risk rationale column to the CSV. Score methodology: data access scope, region, SOC2/ISO compliance, vendor lock-in, and historical security posture. Expect completed scorecard by EOD 2026-11-18.

- Embeddings: default behavior in Hosted = ephemeral ephemeral-by-default. Persistent embedding storage is off unless a customer explicitly enables it via a configuration flag in the console and it is captured in the contract. We will mark the console toggle and a configuration API in the annex.

- Telemetry retention: baseline telemetry retention is 30 days for raw traces and 12 months for aggregated metrics by default. We can shorten or lengthen retention via contract and offer a nil-retention option for sensitive customers. Aggregated metrics are NOT shared with third-party analytics vendors by default; we use an internal analytics pipeline. Any sharing is documented and requires contractual consent.

- KMS / key custody model (summary):
  * Hosted: envelope encryption model where customer may provide a customer-managed data key (BYOK). Redwood stores only wrapped keys; we rotate our wrapping keys per internal policy. For customers who use BYOK, the unwrapped data key material is never exposed to Redwood.
  * Dedicated: customers may run a dedicated KMS in their cloud account and we integrate via standard KMS APIs — Redwood has no ability to extract unwrapped keys.
  * Private/on-prem: HSM-backed key custody available; keys remain under customer control.

I can attach our KMS attestation PDF after legal triage. We will also prepare the subcontractor notification clause (30-day notice) language for the DPA annex.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
